sentences.text:
_ _ _ _
 Mr. Nitin Gaware-Patil with Mr. Divyesh K. Jain for the Petitioner.

Mr. Bapusaheb B. Dahiphale, Agp for Respondent No.4/State.
 __________
 Coram : Sandeep V. Marne, J.
Date : 07 March 2026.
P.C.:
1.

The Petition challenges orders dated 14 June 2018 and 13 December 2021 passed by the learned Civil Judge Senior Division, Alibag, directing payment of share of Respondent Nos.1 to 4 in the compensation in respect of the acquired land.
It appears that after the land was acquired, the Petitioner and Respondent Nos.1 to 4 jointly filed Land Acquisition Reference No.779 of 2000 for enhancement of compensation.
The compensation was enhanced in the Land Acquisition Reference (LAR) vide order dated 31 January 2011.
Respondent Nos.1 to 4 are sisters of the Petitioner.

They were advised to file Application under Order XXI, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure,
1908 (the Code) for payment of their share in the compensation.

The Petitioner opposed the Application interalia on the ground that the Respondents-sisters had agreed to relinquish their claim in respect of the compensation against k 2/3 53 wp 10612.23 as.doc payment of amount of Rs.10,00,000/- each.
The Trial Court has proceeded to direct payment of 1/5th share to each of the four sisters leaving 1/5th share for the Petitioner.
2. Mr. Gaware-Patil, the learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner raises issue of jurisdiction.

He submits that the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 contemplate adjudication of disputes Ravindra Uddhav Patil vs Tulsabai Namdev Mhatre And Ors on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5509671/
1 relating to apportionment only under Section 18 or under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.

sentences.text: He would submit that a party creating dispute relating to apportionment cannot file Execution Application under Order XXI, Rule 11 of the Code.
However, this objection to jurisdiction appears to have been raised for the first time before me.
The same was apparently not raised before the Trial Court.

Even in the present Petition, the ground is not specifically raised and it is vaguely stated in ground clause (x) that the Court did not have jurisdiction to entertain Application relating to apportionment.
The real aim of the Petitioner in setting at naught the impugned orders is to ensure denial of any share in the compensation to the sisters.
He claims that sisters have 'agreed to relinquish' their claims/shares in the amount of compensation.
He expects the sisters to file a separate Suit for claiming their shares in the compensation granted for the acquired land.
Petitioner thus desires to create maximum possible difficulties for the sisters so as to ensure that someday they stop prosecuting any proceedings for claiming shares in the compensation.

Considering this conduct of the Petitioner,
this Court is not inclined to exercise extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of India in favour of the Petitioner.
Also of relevance is the fact that the first impugned order is passed on 14 June 2018 and the present Petition is filed on 18 February 2023.
Even correction in the order dated 14 June 2018 is effected by order dated 13 December 2021.

If at all Petitioner had any valid objection to jurisdiction,
he ought to have challenged order dated 14 June 2018 within a reasonable time.
The share of Respondent Nos.1 to 4 in the compensation has long since been disbursed.
This is yet another reason why this Court is not inclined to entertain the present Petition at this distant point of time.

This Court is also satisfied about the ultimate conclusion of the proceedings where brother (Petitioner) and four sisters (Respondent Nos.1 to 4) are ensured 1/5th share each in the amount of compensation.
No interference is therefore warranted in the impugned order.
Writ Petition is accordingly rejected.

4. It is however clarified that in the event the Petitioner wants to assert his claim in respect of entire amount of compensation, it would be open for him to institute a declaratory suit to that effect.
(SANDEEP V. MARNE, J.)
